name: Moon Base / pressurized rover
note: Challenge: oxygen 'likely 30% or greater', pressure '10.2 psi or less', between spacesuit and Earth values. The outer bounds here are the spacesuit values.
source: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge page, Flame in Freefall (Potential Considerations)

gravity.label: Moon gravity, about 1/6 of Earth's
gravity.source: NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet: 'Surface gravity (m/s2) 1.62 9.80 0.165' (Moon, Earth, ratio); science.nasa.gov/moon/facts: 'the gravity on the surface of the Moon is one-sixth of Earth's'

name: Moon Base (NASA Exploration Air)
note: NASA's current exploration atmosphere is 8.2 psia with 34% O2: 'After re-evaluation in 2012, the 8/32 environment was altered to 8.2 psia and 34% O2' (evidence report, p. 4), which it calls 'the current 8.2 psia habitat pressure with 34% O2' (p. 29). The box is NASA's control band of +-0.2 psia and +-2.0% O2 (NASA/TP-2010-216134, p. 11). That report set the band for its own 2010 recommendations; applying it to 8.2 / 34 is our step, not NASA's.
source: NASA Evidence Report: Risk of Hypoxia from the Exploration Atmosphere (2015), pp. 4 and 29; NASA/TP-2010-216134, p. 11

gravity.label: Moon gravity, about 1/6 of Earth's
gravity.source: NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet: 'Surface gravity (m/s2) 1.62 9.80 0.165' (Moon, Earth, ratio); science.nasa.gov/moon/facts: 'the gravity on the surface of the Moon is one-sixth of Earth's'

name: Space Station (ISS)
note: '...International Space Station (ISS) program have operated at an Earth-equivalent sea level atmosphere of 14.7 psia and 21% O2' (evidence report, p. 5). The box is NASA's control band of +-0.2 psia and +-2.0% O2 around it (NASA/TP-2010-216134, p. 11); applying that band here is our step, not NASA's. Same air as Earth sea level, so the same tests fall in both.
source: NASA Evidence Report: Risk of Hypoxia from the Exploration Atmosphere (2015), p. 5; NASA OCHMO-TB-003 Habitable Atmosphere, p. 8; NASA/TP-2010-216134, p. 11

gravity.label: Microgravity
gravity.source: NASA PSI records: every investigation with tests in these tables is a 'Microgravity Investigation' flown on the International Space Station or a Cygnus cargo craft

name: Spacesuit

name: Earth sea level
note: Pressure from the challenge page (14.7 psi). 21% O2 at 14.7 psia is NASA's 'Earth-equivalent sea level atmosphere' (evidence report, p. 5). The box is NASA's control band of +-0.2 psia and +-2.0% O2 around it (NASA/TP-2010-216134, p. 11); applying that band here is our step, not NASA's.
source: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge page, Flame in Freefall (Potential Considerations); NASA Evidence Report: Risk of Hypoxia from the Exploration Atmosphere (2015), p. 5; NASA/TP-2010-216134, p. 11
